Obesity is a risk factor for the development of several cancers, including breast, colon, and gynecologic carcinomas (1,2). Recent evidence indicates that obesity not only is associated with carcinogenesis but also influences cancer prognosis. For example, obesity has been linked to poorer outcomes in breast (3,4) and colon (5,6) cancers, whereas favorable prognoses have been reported among obese patients with gastric (7) or renal (8) cancers.
